excerpt: Nubank (Nu Holdings, NYSE: NU) is Latin America's largest digital bank, with 139 million customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. It earned more than $1 billion in a quarter for the first time in Q2 2026.
content:
Nubank is a digital bank run through a phone app, offering credit cards, deposit accounts and lending in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Its parent, Nu Holdings Ltd., describes itself as the largest digital bank in Latin America and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker NU. Its About page says it serves more than 140 million customers and has more than 10,000 employees from over 50 nationalities, with a mission to fight complexity and empower people.

David Vélez is Nubank's founder and global CEO. In its second-quarter 2026 results, published on 13 August 2026, Nu said it had added about 4 million customers in the quarter to reach 139 million: almost 118 million in Brazil, 15.8 million in Mexico (16 million by July) and more than 5 million in Colombia. Quarterly net income passed $1 billion for the first time, up 49% year on year on a currency-neutral basis, and return on equity was 33%. Vélez said Nu had just launched its bank in Mexico, becoming the country's largest digital bank, and was adding a full banking licence to its operations in Brazil. He also highlighted NuFormer, the company's own AI foundation model for financial behaviour, which it uses for underwriting, customer service and growth decisions.

For customers in Brazil, Nubank's credit card has no annual fee (sem anuidade), its site says, and is managed in the app; there is also a secured card option where money you set aside in a savings box becomes your card limit. Fees and rates for other products are listed in the app and on Nubank's sites for each country.

This profile draws on Nu's own pages and results release. It is not investment advice. We have not tested the products, and nothing here is paid placement.
